        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

          },
          "endPosition": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "- Stores &amp; caches:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)\n  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (last locations + reverse geocode queue)\n  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached &#96;MKRoute&#96; by device &amp; transport; distance-based validity)\n- Utilities:\n  - &#96;thisDeviceIDManager&#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\n  - &#96;Haptic&#96; (success/warning/error feedback)\n\n### Key Dependencies\n- **CodeScanner**: QR code scanning functionality\n- **MiataruAPIClient** (via local &#96;Libraries/MiataruClientSwift&#96;): Miataru protocol client\n- **QRCode**: QR code generation\n- **SwiftImageReadWrite**: Image handling utilities\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n### Code Organization\n- **Views**: Keep UI logic minimal, delegate to managers\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data persistence\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI's built-in data binding\n- **Assets**: Organize by platform and feature\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- Unit tests for managers and business logic\n- UI tests for critical user flows\n- Test on multiple device types (iPhone, iPad)\n- Verify location permission flows\n\n### Debugging Tips\n- Use Xcode's location simulation for testing\n- Monitor battery usage during development\n- Test background/foreground transitions\n- Verify privacy compliance\n - Test deep links: &#96;miataru://&lt;DEVICE_ID&gt;&#96; (Simulator: &#96;xcrun simctl openurl booted miataru://ABCDEF...&#96;)\n\n## Common Development Tasks\n\n### Adding New Features\n1. Create view in appropriate platform folder\n2. Add manager if business logic is needed\n3. Update settings if user preferences are involved\n4. Add localization strings\n5. Test on all target platforms\n\n### Location Permission Handling\n- Always check authorization status before requesting\n- Provide clear user feedback\n- Handle denied permissions gracefully\n- Respect user's privacy choices\n\n### Settings Management\n- Use &#96;SettingsManager&#96; for all user preferences\n- Observe changes and update UI accordingly\n- Provide sensible defaults\n- Validate user input\n - Register defaults from &#96;Settings.bundle/Root.plist&#96; via &#96;SettingsManager.registerDefaultsFromSettingsBundle()&#96;",

        "contents": "- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)\n  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (latest device locations + reverse geocoded placemarks)\n  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached routes keyed by device/transport; distance threshold validation)\n- Utilities:\n  - &#96;thisDeviceIDManager&#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\n  - &#96;Haptic&#96; (feedback utilities)\n\n## 🔑 Key Features\n\n### Location Management\n- **Privacy-First**: User controls all location sharing\n- **Battery Optimized**: High-accuracy foreground; significant-change background\n- **Permission Handling**: Staged requests (WhenInUse → Always when opted-in)\n- **Background Support**: Significant-change updates\n\n### Device Management\n- **Multi-Device**: Track multiple devices\n- **Group Support**: Organize devices into groups\n- **QR Code Sharing**: Share own device, scan to add others\n- **Deep Link**: &#96;miataru://&lt;DEVICE_ID&gt;&#96; adds devices via sheet\n\n### User Experience\n- **Onboarding Flow**: Guided setup (iPhone/iPad-optimized)\n- **Settings Control**: Comprehensive preferences via SettingsManager\n- **Error Handling**: Transient overlays\n- **Localization**: German, English, and Japanese\n\n## 📱 Platform-Specific Considerations\n\n### iPhone\n- Touch-optimized interface\n- Location permission workflows\n- Deep-link and QR onboarding\n- Battery optimization features\n\n### iPad\n- Larger screen layouts\n- Split view support\n- Enhanced device management\n- Optimized for productivity\n\n### Mac\n- Not currently targeted (Mac directory hosts onboarding previews only)\n\n## 🛠️ Development Guidelines\n\n### Code Organization\n- **Views**: Minimal UI logic, delegate to managers\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI data binding\n- **Assets**: Organized by platform and feature\n\n### State Management\n- Use ObservableObject for view models\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\n- Handle app lifecycle changes\n- Manage user preferences reactively\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- Unit tests for business logic\n- UI tests for critical flows",

        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 18260,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The persistent lastOpenedDeviceID from a prior session can conflict with device ID from openURL at cold start, causing initial navigation to the old device before switching to the URL device. This likely leads to the new device from the URL not properly appearing as expected.**Tracing app launch handling**\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 18264,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The app loads lastOpenedDeviceID from defaults first and auto-navigates there, but openURL sets it to a different device afterward. Meanwhile, scenePhase changes to inactive clear lastOpenedDeviceID early, possibly overwriting the URL-set device before navigation updates, causing the app to show the wrong device on start.**Analyzing device ID lifecycle and URL handling**\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 18268,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The core issue is likely that on cold launch, &amp;amp;#96;.onOpenURL&amp;amp;#96; may not be called promptly or at all, so handling the URL in AppDelegate’s launch options and &amp;amp;#96;application(_:open:)&amp;amp;#96; can reliably capture deep links early. Syncing that with the app state to update lastOpenedDeviceID or show the add-device sheet should fix missed deep links without major refactoring.\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 18296,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The deep link sets lastOpenedDeviceID but map view's onAppear can overwrite it with the old ID before navigation updates trigger, causing stale navigation. To fix, handle scenePhase .active to enforce navigationPath update from lastOpenedDeviceID after app becomes foreground, ensuring navigation sync even if openURL arrives late or views are already rendered.&amp;amp;lt;/details&amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;/think&amp;amp;gt;\\\"\""
                },

              "file": "./.specstory/history/2026-01-08_15-35Z-map-widget-device-view-conflict.md",
              "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1217,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The persistent lastOpenedDeviceID from a prior session can conflict with device ID from openURL at cold start, causing initial navigation to the old device before switching to the URL device. This likely leads to the new device from the URL not properly appearing as expected.**Tracing app launch handling**\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1221,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The app loads lastOpenedDeviceID from defaults first and auto-navigates there, but openURL sets it to a different device afterward. Meanwhile, scenePhase changes to inactive clear lastOpenedDeviceID early, possibly overwriting the URL-set device before navigation updates, causing the app to show the wrong device on start.**Analyzing device ID lifecycle and URL handling**\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1229,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The core issue is likely that on cold launch, &amp;#96;.onOpenURL&amp;#96; may not be called promptly or at all, so handling the URL in AppDelegate’s launch options and &amp;#96;application(_:open:)&amp;#96; can reliably capture deep links early. Syncing that with the app state to update lastOpenedDeviceID or show the add-device sheet should fix missed deep links without major refactoring.\""
                },

                {
                  "lineNumber": 1327,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm checking how the map view uses lastOpenedDeviceID from SettingsManager to navigate on openURL and whether it reads the stored setting efficiently, possibly only partially reading the file.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1348,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm checking &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96; to verify how &amp;#96;lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96; is used for navigation, aiming to adjust &amp;#96;openURL&amp;#96; logic to open an existing device view instead of triggering add-device flow when launching from a widget.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1352,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm updating openURL to set lastOpenedDeviceID when a known device is opened, triggering navigation without onboarding.                 },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1639,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Issue: deeplink sets &amp;#96;lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96;, but SwiftUI may restore navigation before the deeplink runs, so the restored state overrides it. Ensuring deeplinks take precedence by clearing any existing navigation state and forcing navigation to the deeplink device. Updating both iPhone and iPad views:\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1655,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"+                 // This allows deeplinks to override the restoration by setting lastOpenedDeviceID\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1675,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"-                 // This allows deeplinks to override the restoration by setting lastOpenedDeviceID\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1796,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The lastOpenedDeviceID is cleared when the app moves to inactive or background with an empty navigation path, possibly resetting after OnOpenURL sets it to B. The likely cause of opening device A instead of B on launch is that lastOpenedDeviceID persists as A from the last session and navigation happens before OnOpenURL updates it to B. The mismatch may relate to onDisappear not being called on termination, leaving lastOpenedDeviceID stale until overridden.**Analyzing URL handling conflict with state restoration**\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1800,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The app likely attaches onOpenURL only to the main WindowGroup, possibly missing handling in new iPad windows, which may block deep link responses when the map view was last open. The saved lastOpenedDeviceID persisting across sessions may cause autopush logic to override deep link navigation, especially if onDisappear clears lastOpenedDeviceID inconsistently on app termination. Next, confirming other onOpenURL uses and app scene behavior will clarify whether deep link handling or state restoration order causes the bug.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""

                {
                  "lineNumber": 2613,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Interestingly, .onAppear isn't retriggered, and there’s an .onChange code resetting its state when lastOpenedDeviceID becomes nil, but that doesn’t solve the issue. It's possible that the navigation might auto-select lastID if the app is restored from a previous run. However, the user insists they chose Device A on a cold start, so it shouldn't auto-restore.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2617,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The goal is to adjust how and when lastOpenedDeviceID updates occur, possibly ensuring it clears earlier when leaving the map view, to avoid unintended navigation behavior and ensure it only restores on true cold starts. Additionally, tracking when the app was launched can help clarify whether the lastOpenedID should even be set. I need to check the interactions in other views to identify any additional triggers.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2621,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm noticing that the list's onAppear seems to trigger earlier than expected; it happens when the list appears, not necessarily when I tap within it. The auto-restore feature activates when returning from a previous screen, but I need to ensure that &amp;#96;settings.lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96; gets cleared to prevent unwanted auto-restore. It might be better to check the navigation from the top view during &amp;#96;DevicesView.onAppear&amp;#96;. Another possible solution is to implement a flag in the AppState to track if restoration has occurred this launch.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2625,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm reviewing the scenario where the map view appears, and when &amp;#96;lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96; is set to A during its onAppear method, then gets reset to nil on disappear. The issue arises because &amp;#96;didAutoNavigateFromSavedDevice&amp;#96; is set to true at cold starts but doesn't change when navigating manually through a NavigationLink. This means that returning to the list may incorrectly trigger auto-restore. I think we should set &amp;#96;didAutoNavigateFromSavedDevice&amp;#96; to true when a user manually selects a row. I’ll need to consider how to detect manual navigation properly.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2637,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm noticing an issue where pressing back brings me to A and then back to the list. The root cause seems to be the auto-restore of lastOpenedDeviceID in the iPhone_DevicesView. This should ideally only occur once during a cold start but shouldn't trigger when coming back from a map view. The logic in place has some resetting conflicts, leading to unexpected behavior. It's clear there's a race condition involved here, and that needs further investigation.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2645,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I can use @SceneStorage or @AppStorage to track navigation across app sessions. A straightforward solution is to avoid resetting didAutoNavigateFromSavedDevice in .onChange and only set it to false when the app becomes active for the first time. Another idea is to adjust DeviceMapView.onDisappear to keep lastOpenedDeviceID rather than clearing it. But to prevent autopush to the last device every time the list appears, I’ll only auto-navigate if lastOpenedDeviceID is set and it’s the first appearance after launch. I'll implement a @State variable called hasAppearedOnce for this purpose.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2649,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to examine how lastOpenedDeviceID is managed when navigating away from the DeviceMapView. Currently, it clears the ID upon leaving the detail view, which prevents restoring it during a cold start. The user wants to restore the last displayed device after a restart, but the clearing mechanism disrupts this. I’ll propose not clearing lastOpenedDeviceID on disappear and ensuring that autopush only triggers once when the view first appears. Additionally, I should eliminate unnecessary resets of the didAutoNavigateFromSavedDevice variable to fix the issue of repeated autopush.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2653,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm looking at a medium level of changes across multiple files, so I’ll create a todo list to keep track. First, I need to fix the iPhone_DevicesView auto-restore logic to ensure it only triggers once and remove any race conditions. I'll stop clearing lastOpenedDeviceID on DeviceMapView.onDisappear to let the restoration persist. There's also an optional step to avoid clearing the ID when the app goes to the background. I'll check the SettingsManager to see if there's a property that handles writing back lastOpenedDeviceID, since it must be persisted in UserDefaults to effectively restore across app restarts.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2670,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to ensure that the app triggers correctly on a fresh start. I'll initialize hasAutoNavigatedFromSavedID to false and set it to true on the first appear. However, double transitions might still happen if lastOpenedDeviceID is non-nil. So, I’ll manage the state carefully upon .onDisappear. I think it’s acceptable to maintain hasAutoNavigated as true for the entire session, meaning auto-restore only occurs on cold starts. I’ll implement these changes in the iPhone_DevicesView to remove potential double pushes. \""
                },

                  "lineNumber": 11600,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The issue likely arises because the device map view’s onAppear resets lastOpenedDeviceID shortly after onOpenURL sets it, causing the deep-linked device to be overridden by the previously stored device ID during app launch. Adjusting the initialization and update order around lastOpenedDeviceID and navigationPath may resolve the conflict.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 11604,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The deep link sets lastOpenedDeviceID but map view's onAppear can overwrite it with the old ID before navigation updates trigger, causing stale navigation. To fix, handle scenePhase .active to enforce navigationPath update from lastOpenedDeviceID after app becomes foreground, ensuring navigation sync even if openURL arrives late or views are already rendered.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    // Access the horizontal size class from the environment to distinguish between compact (iPhone) and regular (iPad) layouts\n    @Environment(\\.horizontalSizeClass) var horizontalSizeClass\n    // Binding to control whether the onboarding is presented\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    // Tracks the current page in the onboarding flow\n    @State private var currentPage = 0\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        #if os(macOS)\n        // Use the macOS-specific onboarding container view\n        MacOnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        #else\n        if horizontalSizeClass == .compact {\n            // Show the iPhone-specific onboarding container view for compact width devices\n            iPhone_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        } else {\n            // Show the iPad-specific onboarding container view for regular width devices\n            iPad_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        }\n        #endif\n    }\n}\n\n// Preview provider for SwiftUI previews\nstruct OnboardingContainerView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n    @State static var isPresented = true\n    static var previews: some View {\n        OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented)\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPad_OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    @Binding var currentPage: Int\n    \n    private var pages: [AnyView] {\n        [\n            AnyView(iPhone_1_OnboardingWelcomeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_2_OnboardingLocationPermissionView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_3_OnboardingServerView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_4_OnboardingLocationHistoryView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_5_OnboardingQRcodeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_6_OnboardingDoneView(onFinish: {\n                UserDefaults.standard.hasCompletedOnboarding = true\n                isPresented = false\n            }))\n        ]\n    }\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        VStack {\n            TabView(selection: $currentPage) {\n                ForEach(0..&lt;pages.count, id: \\.self) { index in\n                    pages[index]\n                        .tag(index)\n                }\n            }\n            .tabViewStyle(PageTabViewStyle())\n            .indexViewStyle(PageIndexViewStyle(backgroundDisplayMode: .always))\n        }\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground))\n        .ignoresSafeArea()\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground).ignoresSafeArea())\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    // Beispiel-Bindings für die Vorschau\n    @Previewable @State var isPresented = true\n    @Previewable @State var currentPage = 0\n    return iPad_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n}",

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },

            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",
            "lineNumber": 6

          {
            "text": "- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "text": "- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Location Tracking",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 28
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.41027000546455383

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**.                 },

                  "lineNumber": 1348,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm checking &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96; to verify how &amp;#96;lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96; is used for navigation, aiming to adjust &amp;#96;openURL&amp;#96; logic to open an existing device view instead of triggering add-device flow when launching from a widget.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1425,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"| Web Search Results |  | Um sicherzustellen, dass beim Neustart der App auf dem iPad immer die &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; angezeigt wird und nicht ein zuvor geöffnetes zusätzliches Fenster, können Sie die automatische Wiederherstellung des Anwendungszustands deaktivieren. Dies verhindert, dass iOS beim Neustart der App den vorherigen Zustand wiederherstellt und somit unerwünschte Fenster öffnet.&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;In SwiftUI-Apps, die das neue App-Lifecycle-Modell verwenden, können Sie einen &amp;#96;UIApplicationDelegate&amp;#96; hinzufügen, um die Zustandswiederherstellung zu steuern. Obwohl Apple empfiehlt, den App-Delegate nur bei Bedarf zu verwenden ([eclecticlight.co](https://eclecticlight.co/2024/04/17/swiftui-on-macos-life-cycle-and-appdelegate/?utm_source=openai)), ist dies in Ihrem Fall gerechtfertigt.&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;Hier ist, wie Sie vorgehen können:&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;1. **AppDelegate-Klasse erstellen**: Definieren Sie eine Klasse, die dem &amp;# [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2414,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"es kann passieren dass das falsche fenster restored wird/initialisiert wird. Es soll immer auf dem iPad das MiataruRootView gezeigt werden bei neustart/kaltstart\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2422,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to confirm that &amp;#96;.handlesExternalEvents&amp;#96; indicates a scene only responds to external events defined by activity type or URL scheme. According to Apple’s documentation, if I pass an empty set, external events won’t activate the scene. However, it seems I want the opposite, ensuring the secondary group isn't created automatically. The &amp;#96;WindowGroup(for:)&amp;#96; may still get created if the system is trying to restore it, but disabling restore in AppDelegate should help. Still, the user experiences wrong window initialization, possibly due to how I've structured the &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96;.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2426,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to modify the second &amp;#96;WindowGroup&amp;#96; so that it only responds to the URL scheme \\\"miataru\\\" and the path \\\"device\\\" or something similar. Currently, our &amp;#96;onOpenURL&amp;#96; uses the scheme &amp;#96;miataru://{deviceID}&amp;#96; without a path. For &amp;#96;.handlesExternalEvents&amp;#96;, it looks like the matching primarily involves URL hosts. Although we disable restoration to prevent automatic creation, I wonder if making the second group &amp;#96;providesDefaultScene: false&amp;#96; would help. Since we want the MiataruRootView on iPad but don't want the second group auto-creating, I'll check the codebase for any &amp;#96;openWindow&amp;#96; usages.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2434,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I want to check if the primary &amp;#96;WindowGroup&amp;#96; should have its &amp;#96;.restorationBehavior(.disabled)&amp;#96; set. We already disabled restoration in the AppDelegate, so it's probably fine to add this for clarity. The goal is to ensure that &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; shows on a cold start, and with restoration disabled throughout the app, the primary group will appear as expected. I’ll implement patch lines around 100-107 and apply the necessary changes, but I don't think &amp;#96;.windowResizability(.automatic)&amp;#96; is needed here.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2438,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I’m going to update the secondary typed window scene to explicitly disable its restoration so it won’t be initialized or restored on cold start, ensuring the iPad always shows &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96; first. Then I’ll run a quick linter check on the file.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2446,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"- I’ll ensure the secondary window scene can’t be restored/auto-created so iPad always launches to &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96;. Lint looks clean.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2633,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm thinking of a way to make the auto-restore logic more straightforward in &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView.onAppear&amp;#96;. I could set it to only restore if the app is being launched for the first time by checking if &amp;#96;store.devices&amp;#96; is loaded and using a flag like &amp;#96;isColdStart&amp;#96; from AppState. Since AppState isn't currently accessible in &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, I could inject it using &amp;#96;environmentObject&amp;#96;. I see that it’s passed down through &amp;#96;MiataruRootView&amp;#96;, so I should check how that is structured.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },

Fixed the iPad widget deeplink issue.

## The Problem
On iPad, tapping a widget sets `lastOpenedDeviceID`, but the app didn’t switch to the Devices tab. If you were on Groups, QR, or Settings, the device wouldn’t open because `iPad_DevicesView` wasn’t visible.

## The Solution
Added the same tab switching logic used in `iPhone_RootView` to `iPad_RootView`:
1. Added `@State private var selectedTab = 0` to track the selected tab
2. Added `.tag()` modifiers to each tab item
3. Bound the `TabView` to `selectedTab`
4. Added an `.onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID)` handler that switches to tab 0 (Devices) when a deeplink is received

When a widget is tapped on iPad:
1. The deeplink is handled and `lastOpenedDeviceID` is set
2. The app switches to the Devices tab
3. `iPad_DevicesView` responds to the `lastOpenedDeviceID` change and selects the correct device in the split view

This matches the iPhone behavior and ensures widget deeplinks work on iPad.

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",
